newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa cutting management by 10 percent.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa cutting management by 10 percent.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG said Wednesday it will shed at least 10 percent of management staff as it prepares for full liberalisation of the European aviation market this year.

The move, which marks the completion of a restructuring begun in 1994, will take effect April 1, coinciding with the implementation of an "open skies" agreement which will allow airlines to compete for all routes in Europe.
Lufthansa, due to be fully privatised at the end of the year, said it will group all its passenger services in a separate division which will act as a profit centre with its own management board.
The airline said in a statement it would be creating a wide-ranging passenger division under which sales, marketing, network management, flight and staff operations would be brought together.

The division's six-member management will report to the group board, which will be free to concentrate on steering the airline as a whole, ensuring "greater market proximity, flexibility and homegeneity of leadership," the statement said.
The announcement scotched media speculation that the airline was planning to turn its scheduled passenger services into a separate subsidiary.
A source close to the company said aviation authorities would not have approved such a spin-off because Lufthansa needed to retain its legal status as a scheduled airline.

The addition of a management layer at Lufthansa contrasts with a reorganization at industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG, which said last month it was scrapping the management board of car subsidiary Mercedes-Benz AG in an internal merger.

Analysts gave a cautious welcome to the changes but added the savings were likely to be relatively small and that Lufthansa's share could come under pressure when it publishes what will almost certainly be weaker earnings for 1996.
